daily_brief: The day's most significant developments center on shifting dynamics in two ongoing crises. President Trump announced he would cancel planned strikes on Iran after regional allies requested a pause, claiming the 'perimeters' of a deal have been agreed that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and address Iran's nuclear program [BBC, France 24, Financial Times]. The announcement came after reports that the US and Israel had been planning intensive strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure. In Europe, the Ceuta migration crisis has triggered an EU emergency meeting scheduled for Tuesday after Italy suspended Schengen arrangements with Spain—a move backed by Finland and Denmark—following the arrival of some 60,000 migrants at Spain's North African enclave [BBC, The Guardian, France 24]. At least 67 people died in the crossing, and Spain has begun installing floating barriers while condemning what it called 'selfish, polarising and unlawful' reactions from EU partners. Meanwhile, a bombing at a Moscow restaurant killed three people including the female bomber [France 24, Al Jazeera], Hungary announced the shutdown of its sole nuclear plant due to record-low Danube water levels [The Hindu], and UEFA publicly declared it had lost confidence in FIFA president Gianni Infantino following the collapse of his World Cup privatization plan [RFI, BBC].

top_stories.headline: Trump Cancels Planned Iran Strikes, Claims Deal Parameters Agreed
bullets: President Trump announced on Truth Social that he has cancelled planned US strikes on Iran after being asked by Iran and Middle Eastern allies to hold off while deal parameters are finalized
The proposed deal would include immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat, according to Trump
CBS News had earlier reported that the US and Israel were planning intensive joint strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure, possibly throughout the weekend
Iran's acting defence minister responded that Tehran views all threats as 'real and credible' and would use them to increase military readiness and strengthen deterrence

top_stories.headline: EU Calls Emergency Meeting as Ceuta Migration Crisis Sparks Intra-European Tensions
bullets: Approximately 60,000 migrants crossed into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco beginning July 30, with at least 67 confirmed dead from drowning and crushing
Italy suspended its Schengen free-movement arrangement with Spain, backed by Finland and Denmark, while 22 EU member states signed a joint letter calling for coordinated border action
Spain condemned reactions as 'selfish, polarising and unlawful' and announced over 48,000 migrants had returned to Morocco within 48 hours
Spanish authorities began installing a 500-metre floating barrier on the sea border with Morocco as EU interior ministers prepare for Tuesday emergency talks

top_stories.headline: Three Killed in Moscow Restaurant Bombing; Female Attacker Among Dead
bullets: A homemade explosive device detonated at an Italian restaurant in Kudrinskaya Square, Moscow, killing three people and injuring 21
The dead include the female bomber who attempted to carry the device into the restaurant, a security guard who stopped her, and a patron
Russian authorities have not identified the target of the attack and say the investigation is ongoing
Russia's national anti-terrorism committee confirmed the incident was a bombing

top_stories.headline: UEFA and Concacaf Publicly Condemn Infantino Leadership After World Cup Sale Plan Collapses
bullets: FIFA abandoned plans to sell a 20% stake in World Cup commercial rights to private investors after backlash from regional confederations who said they were not consulted
UEFA stated the 'current Fifa leadership has not only lost Uefa's confidence but also that of many other members of the football family'
Concacaf called for a 'full review of this leadership' describing the proposals as 'a symptom of leadership that has stopped putting football first'
The controversy comes as Infantino seeks re-election for a fourth term at the FIFA Congress in March 2027

top_stories.headline: Hungary Announces First-Ever Shutdown of Sole Nuclear Plant Due to Record-Low Danube Levels
bullets: Hungary's Paks nuclear power plant, which provides about one-third of the country's electricity, will shut down completely for the first time in its 44-year history
Record-low Danube River water levels caused by prolonged drought and successive heatwaves since May have made cooling operations impossible
Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced the shutdown would be complete by Monday after output fell to 240 megawatts
Temperatures in Hungary are forecast to reach 42°C this week, potentially matching the national record set earlier this summer
